story_text:
[画像: Flic Cue held in a hand. You say: out of oat milk, dentist Thursday, call Mom back. Cue files it in the shopping list, calendar and reminders]
Flic Cue is an AI voice button. Say what's on your mind, and Cue puts it in the right place.
[画像: A black Flic Cue. Built in: shopping list, calendar, notes, reminders, to-dos, email drafts and more. Connected: ChatGPT, Claude, your own agent, Grok Bot, Home Assistant, open SDK and much more]
[画像: Estimated shipping February 2027. Built on our award-winning Flic Duo, with a new circuit board and a microphone. Certification testing complete, paperwork being finalized. Parts for the first 3,000 Cues already bought. Trial run of 100 units starts tomorrow, Friday 6 November]
## How it works.
[画像: How it works: hold, speak, done. Cue only listens while you hold it, so one battery lasts up to 2 years]
Flic Cue is two things working together: the button you hold, and the Cue app on your phone or Flic Hub. Your voice goes over Bluetooth to the app, which works out what you mean and where it belongs. You don't open anything.
## Say it. It's handled.
[画像: You say it, Cue handles it: a message to Sam, a reminder, a note, an email draft and a baby log]
Say several things at once, and Cue sorts them into the right places.
Small tasks shouldn't need your phone.
[画像: Adding milk to the shopping list: 20 minutes later with your phone, 3 seconds with Flic Cue]
Most of the time you reach for your phone, it's to get one small thing out of your head. Then the phone keeps you, and your kids notice every time. Say it to Cue instead: hold, speak, done, and they get you, not the back of your phone.
Text without picking up your phone.
[画像: Without Cue a woman types a message on her phone while driving; with Cue she holds the Cue on her dashboard and says it]
Hold Cue and say the message and who it's for. It's sent, and your phone stays where it is. In the car, Cue sits on the dashboard with the mount add-on.
## Set up in seconds.
[画像: Three steps: get the free Cue app for iOS or Android, add your Cue over Bluetooth, then hold it and talk. That's it. Go advanced whenever you're ready.]
## From the team that has already shipped over 1 million smart buttons.
[画像: The Flic team in Stockholm, Sweden, and every Flic Kickstarter shipped: 26,869 backers across four campaigns]
[画像: What the press said about earlier Flic products]
That's us: Shortcut Labs in Stockholm, Sweden, the people who made every Flic. Press quotes are about earlier Flic products.
## Back it from $69.
[画像: Early Bird sold out. Now from $69, 22% off the $89 store price]
## Why Flic Cue
[画像: Why Flic Cue: simple to use and wildly configurable, $0 a month, up to 2 years per battery, any language, private by design]
## Start simple. Go further when you want.
The Cue app is the first responder. It handles everyday things on its own, for free, and hands bigger jobs to the agents and tools you connect.
[画像: Everyday things are built in and free. Optionally connect your AI agent, or plug Cue into your own stack]
## How does Cue answer?
[画像: Cue answers always in the app, in your headphones or out loud]
Most of what you say needs no answer: a short beep tells you it landed. For a bigger question you don't sit and wait. Ask now, put Cue away, and two beeps tell you when the answer is ready.
It comes back in three ways, and you can also have it sent on as a text message, an email or a note in apps like Notion.
## Catch the thought, wherever it hits.
[画像: At home Cue waits on its magnetic wall plate; on the go it rides in its clip]
Cue waits on its magnetic wall plate at home. Lift it off and clip it on when you leave. The clip and the wall mount are add-ons, and most homes want more than one Cue: one on you, one by the door, one in the kitchen.
## Let your AI agent do the research.
[画像: Your AI agent does the research: three examples with pros and cons]
Bigger jobs, in seconds: the kind that usually take an evening of open tabs. Say it to Cue, and your AI agent, for example Grok Bot, researches, gathers and sums up the best options with pros and cons.
Connect your own account in the Cue app, and Flic's cloud hands over what you say, cloud to cloud. More agents are coming.
## Lets you know when it's done.
[画像: Beeps: one for got it, two for done, a repeating beep when something needs you]
Start a long task, walk away and know when to come back.
## Every press, logged.
[画像: The Cue app shows what Cue heard, where it went and what it learned]
Cue works with the email, calendar and notes you already keep in the cloud, and you pick the destinations in the Cue app. Everything you say shows up there, with where it went. When Cue isn't sure, it asks. It learns from every correction.
[画像: For power users: gestures, desk and motion control, and building on Cue]
## Every gesture is yours to map.
[画像: Every gesture is yours to map: swipe up, down, left or right to send it somewhere different]
Your hand does the routing, so your voice only has to carry the content. Push, double push and hold on two buttons, swipe four ways, turn and shake, and choose in the Cue app what each one does.
## See it work, on a real prototype.
Oskar, our CTO, with a working prototype at his desk. The desktop features in the video are still experiments and can change.
## Lean back. Run your agents.
[画像: Desktop controls: dictate, shake to undo, swipe to copy, turn to switch apps and windows, keyboard commands by voice]
Pick the agent session by turning Cue, give the next instruction by voice and let the agent get on with it, as in the video above. Cue already drives Claude, Codex and Gemini sessions on your computer.
## A motion controller in your hand.
[画像: Cue as a motion controller: change slides and adjust any value]
Push to start a presentation, and talk to add a note without leaving the stage.
## Everything Flic Duo does, plus voice.
[画像: 200+ integrations in the free Flic app]
## Flic now talks to Home Assistant.
[画像: Turn off the downstairs lights: Home Assistant turns off three rooms]
For the first time, Flic Cue and the Flic buttons you already have connect to Home Assistant, and Cue runs it by voice. It was the integration our waitlist asked for most.
## Build Cue into your own app or project.
[画像: For builders: truly hackable, open SDKs for all Flic products including Flic Cue. SDKs, sample apps and docs; Flic Hub LR Studio for solutions that run without a phone (requires Flic Hub LR); vibe-code ready instructions for AI agents; and an open protocol for any language and any hardware with Bluetooth LE]
Every Flic Cue can be configured and built into your own apps, agents and systems. Build the thing you wish existed, and share it with the community.
## A pledge to work with anything we can.
[画像: Confirmed today: ChatGPT through a custom MCP server, Claude Routines, Grok Bot and OpenClaw through webhooks]
The landscape moves fast. New ways to plug into AI agents appear all the time, and some get shut down. We aim for integrations that work on the lowest tiers possible, though they still need an active subscription with each service.
We'll keep adding support for the next big thing, and with help from the community, the small things too. What works today might not be possible tomorrow. What we can promise is to do everything in our power to make Flic Cue the most versatile voice button on the planet.
## Tech specs.
[画像: Flic Cue tech specs: the inside of Cue with its battery, accelerometer, switches, Bluetooth LE, microphone, buzzer and LED]
## Pick your Cue.
[画像: Flic Cue Early Bird rewards: Single Cue 33% off, Home Bundle 30% off, Double Cue 38% off, Triple Cue 44% off, Large Home Bundle 42% off, XL Bundle 44% off]
## Add-ons: extra Cues, accessories and more Flic.
[画像: Add-ons: an extra Flic Cue for $69 (22% off), a clip, a wall mount, a Cue sticker pack, a silicone sleeve that makes Cue waterproof and a lanyard that needs the Cue clip, plus Flic 2 for $29 (25% off), Flic Twist for $59 (25% off), Flic Hub Mini for $39 (20% off) and the Flic Hub LR upgrade]
Add-ons ship in the same box as your reward, at no extra shipping cost.
## Flic Hub Mini or Flic Hub LR?
[画像: Flic Hub Mini compared with Flic Hub LR]
The Hub Mini is enough for most homes. Every bundle with a hub comes with one, and the Hub LR upgrade swaps it. The Hacker Bundle comes with a Hub LR.
## From launch to your door.
[画像: From launch on 5 November, with trial production ongoing, to estimated shipping in February 2027; some orders may ship in March]
You get an update at every step, and you can talk to us any time in the Flic Discord.
This project is promoted by Jellop, the ad tech power behind the best Kickstarters with 3,500+ successful Kickstarter projects with over $1B raised between them.
risks: Flic Cue is built on Flic Duo, which we’ve been shipping for a year, so the tooling is already made. The circuit board is certified and ready for production, and the main components for the first 3,000 units are already bought and arrive in January, if not earlier. That leaves the practical parts: packaging, logistics and shipping. We’ve delivered four Kickstarter campaigns and more than one million Flic buttons, so we know where delays usually come from and plan for them. If anything moves, you’ll hear it from us first, in an update. Personal agents like Grok Bot and OpenAI dots are run by other companies, which can change their features, prices or availability. Cue’s core features don’t depend on them.

faq.a: Your phone stays in your pocket. Hold Cue, say what's on your mind and let go, and the thought is handled before your phone can pull you in. It puts things where they belong: your shopping list, calendar, messages, notes or AI agent, in any language and in your own words. It only listens while you hold it, and what you say is never used to train AI models. It runs for years on a coin cell you swap yourself, with no charging. And it does everything Flic Duo does, with 200+ integrations in the fre…

We're Shortcut Labs, the Stockholm team behind Flic, and we've shipped more than one million Flic buttons. This is our fifth crowdfunding campaign: Flic, Flic Hub, Flic 2 and Flic Twist had 26,869 backers in total, and all four shipped. Flic Cue is built on Flic Duo, which we've shipped for a year, so the tooling is done and the circuit board is certified. We still support our first button from 2014, and we intend to support Flic Cue for as long as it's reasonably possible.

faq.q: How does Cue know where to put what I say?
faq.a: From your words. "Add oat milk to the shopping list" goes on the list, "Dentist Thursday at nine" goes in your calendar, and "Tell Sam I'm running late" becomes a message to Sam. Every cue lands in the Cue app's log, so you can see what Cue heard and what it did. If it isn't sure, it asks you in the app, for example "Which Sam did you mean?", and it gets better with every correction. Email drafts wait in the app until you send them.

faq.q: Which apps does it work with?
faq.a: The Cue app has its own notes, reminders, to-do lists and shopping lists, so everyday things need no other app. Results can also go out as a text message, an email or a note in apps like Notion, or to your own system through a webhook or MCP. We keep adding more with help from the community, so tell us in the comments which apps you use.

faq.q: Can I use ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or my own AI agent?
faq.a: Yes. Confirmed today: ChatGPT through a custom MCP server and Claude through Routines, with your own subscription to each, and Grok Bot and OpenClaw through webhooks. OpenAI dots works too, outside the EEA, Switzerland and the UK. You can also add your own API key from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google in the Cue app. On your computer, Cue can dictate to Codex, Claude and Gemini sessions. Each button can go to its own agent or model.
No. The Cue app and its core AI models are free. Agents and AI services you connect, like ChatGPT, Claude or Grok Bot, need your own account with them, and some charge for use.

faq.q: Does Flic Cue have a speaker?
faq.a: No. Answers are read out by your phone or in your headphones, and every answer is saved in the Cue app. Cue itself confirms with a beep and its light.

faq.q: Does my phone need to be nearby?
faq.a: Cue sends what you say over Bluetooth to the Cue app on your phone or Flic Hub, up to 50 m indoors. Your phone can stay in your pocket, your bag or the next room. You don't need a Flic Hub.

faq.q: What do the two buttons do?
faq.a: You decide in the Cue app. Hold either one to talk. You can give each button its own job, for example one for notes and lists and one for questions to your AI agent, or send them to different agents. Pushes, double pushes and gestures can run other actions too, just like on Flic Duo.

faq.q: Does it work with Home Assistant, Alexa or Apple Home?
faq.a: Cue's buttons and gestures do, through the free Flic app, where Cue works like a Flic Duo with 200+ integrations, including Home Assistant, Alexa, Sonos, IFTTT and SmartThings. Apple Home needs a Flic Hub LR, and Matter needs a Flic Hub Mini or Hub LR. Voice commands go to the Cue app, not the Flic app, and a webhook can pass what you say on to your own system.

faq.q: I already have Flic buttons. How is Cue different from Flic Duo?
faq.a: Flic Cue is a Flic Duo with a microphone and the Cue app. Same size, same two buttons and gestures, so it does everything Duo does, in the Flic app next to your other buttons and Hubs. And you can talk to it.

faq.q: Is it always listening? What happens to what I say?
faq.a: No. The microphone is on only while you hold a button, and there's no wake word. What you say is never used to train AI models. Flic follows GDPR and deletes your data when you ask. Questions about your data go to support@flic.io.

faq.q: Can I use my own server or a local model?
faq.a: Out of the box, the Cue app uses AI models from cloud providers to understand you. For your own setup, webhooks send what you say to your own endpoint, and MCP is supported. The Flic Cue SDK, coming soon, will let apps connect to Cue directly, as the Flic Duo SDK does today.

faq.q: How long does the battery last?
faq.a: Up to two years with about 4 minutes of talking a day, around 24 ten-second commands. It's a standard CR2032 coin cell you swap yourself, so there's no charging and no cable.
Any language you speak to it in, in your own words.
